CATTLEMAN® SINGLE ACTION REVOLVER AND REVOLVING CARBINE INSTRUCTION MANUAL and safety information — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. (ABSENT — no copyright line printed. The document carries A. Uberti S.p.A.'s registered mark and a disclaimer of liability, but no dated copyright statement.)
cleanIntro: This is A. Uberti's book, published by Taylor's & Co on its own manuals index as the manual for the guns it sells — Taylor's is an importer of Italian replicas and does not print its own name in it. The book is organised by SAFETY SYSTEM rather than by model, and that is the first thing to resolve: it describes four different arrangements (Cattleman II retracting firing pin, hammer safety bar, cylinder base pin safety, transfer bar) and the base pin safety exists ONLY on the Cattleman with a hammer safety bar. The same operation then splits again by frame type. The published strip is short — half cock, gate open, six chambers checked, base pin out, cylinder out — and cleaning is done in that state.

steps.title: Half cock, gate open, one full revolution
steps.action: Move the hammer rearward to the half cock (loading) position and open the loading gate fully. Then rotate the cylinder slowly through ONE COMPLETE REVOLUTION, looking at each of the six chambers in turn through the gate. Only one chamber is visible at a time on a fixed-cylinder single action — there is no swing-out to show you all six at once, which is precisely why the manual asks for a full revolution rather than a glance.
steps.prose: The cylinder will only turn freely at half cock. If it is locked, the hammer is not where you think it is.
steps.quote: Before beginning any cleaning or maintenance procedures, MAKE SURE the revolver is unloaded.
steps.cite: 1873 S.A. CATTLEMAN® SINGLE ACTION REVOLVER AND REVOLVING CARBINE INSTRUCTION MANUAL and safety information — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Cleaning and Maintenance, p.20
steps.warn: To do this, move the hammer rearward to the half cock (loading) position and open the loading gate. Then, slowly rotate the cylinder one complete revolution, take care to ensure each of the six chambers is empty.

steps.title: If any chamber is loaded — the ejector rod, full stroke, every chamber
steps.action: With the hammer at half cock and the gate fully open, press the ejector rod under the barrel rearward to push each cartridge or case out through the gate, let the rod return, rotate to the next chamber and repeat. Operate the rod its FULL length every time — a short stroke leaves a case standing proud in the chamber where it looks ejected and is not. Then turn the cylinder one more complete revolution before you close the gate.
steps.prose: Six chambers, six strokes, then a confirming revolution. That is the manual's sequence and it exists because this action shows you one chamber at a time.
steps.caution: ALWAYS keep your finger out of the trigger guard and off of the trigger while loading and unloading.
steps.quote: You must operate the ejector rod its full length in each chamber to ensure complete cartridge ejection. Once each chamber has been unloaded, slowly rotate the cylinder one more complete revolution, take care to ensure each of the six chambers is now completely empty. Then, and only then, should you close the loading gate.
steps.cite: 1873 S.A. CATTLEMAN® SINGLE ACTION REVOLVER AND REVOLVING CARBINE INSTRUCTION MANUAL and safety information — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Safe Unloading, p.19

steps.title: ⛔ Which of the four safety systems is on YOUR Cattleman
steps.action: Before you follow any procedure in this book, work out which gun you have. It covers four different safety arrangements: the Cattleman II with a retracting firing pin, the Cattleman with a hammer safety bar, the Cattleman with a cylinder base pin safety, and the Cattleman with a transfer bar. The base pin safety is applied ONLY on the version with the hammer safety bar — so if your revolver has no safety bar, that whole chapter is not yours, and its elongated base pin is not a part you have.
steps.prose: One book, four mechanisms, thirteen model designations on the forgings list. The chapter headings are the only thing separating them.
steps.quote: The cylinder base pin safety is applied only on the S.A. Cattleman Revolver with hammer safety bar.
steps.cite: 1873 S.A. CATTLEMAN® SINGLE ACTION REVOLVER AND REVOLVING CARBINE INSTRUCTION MANUAL and safety information — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Safety Systems, p.6
steps.warn: THE CYLINDER BASE PIN SAFETY IS A MANUAL SAFETY. The cylinder base pin safety device will only work if the user properly engages it by carefully following these instructions. This revolver does not have an “automatic” safety; therefore, the safety is not always on and must be engaged by the user.

steps.title: And which frame — Old Model or New Model
steps.action: The second split is the frame. Uberti states that although the elongated base pin works the same way on every model, HOW you move it differs by frame type: on an Old Model or Black Powder frame you LOOSEN the cylinder base pin screw; on a New Model or Prewar frame you DEPRESS a spring-loaded base pin screw. Try to unscrew a spring-loaded screw and you will damage it; try to depress a threaded one and nothing will move.
steps.prose: This same split governs taking the cylinder out, so get it settled before the next step rather than during it.
steps.caution: Old Model / Black Powder frame: loosen the screw. New Model / Prewar frame: depress the spring-loaded screw.
steps.quote: Although the elongated cylinder base pin functions the same way on all models, its movement is accomplished by two different methods depending on the model.
steps.cite: 1873 S.A. CATTLEMAN® SINGLE ACTION REVOLVER AND REVOLVING CARBINE INSTRUCTION MANUAL and safety information — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Safety Systems, p.6

steps.title: Gate open, hammer to half cock
steps.action: The cylinder removal sequence opens the same way as clearing: loading gate open first, then the hammer back to half cock. Doing it in that order means the cylinder is already free to turn when the gate is out of the way, and the gate itself is what the cylinder will come out past.
steps.prose: The gate has to be fully open, not partly. It is the only opening the cylinder can leave through.
steps.quote: REMOVING THE CYLINDER: To remove the cylinder, follow these steps: 1. Open the loading gate. 2. Move the hammer rearward to the half cock (loading) position.
steps.cite: 1873 S.A. CATTLEMAN® SINGLE ACTION REVOLVER AND REVOLVING CARBINE INSTRUCTION MANUAL and safety information — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Cleaning and Maintenance, p.20

steps.title: Base pin screw — your model's way — then the pin out the front
steps.action: Depending on your model, either loosen the cylinder base pin screw or depress the spring-loaded base pin screw, then draw the cylinder base pin forward out of the frame toward the muzzle. Slide it all the way out until it is clear. If the pin will not move, the screw is not fully released — do not pull harder, because the base pin is what the cylinder rotates on and a bent one is a new part.
steps.prose: The pin comes out the FRONT, past the ejector housing. Keep the revolver level so it does not drag.
steps.caution: Which screw you have depends on Old Model / Black Powder frame versus New Model / Prewar frame.
steps.quote: 3. Depending on your model, either loosen the cylinder base pin screw or depress
steps.cite: 1873 S.A. CATTLEMAN® SINGLE ACTION REVOLVER AND REVOLVING CARBINE INSTRUCTION MANUAL and safety information — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Cleaning and Maintenance, p.20

steps.title: Cylinder out through the loading gate side
steps.action: With the base pin fully out, take the cylinder out toward the LOADING GATE side of the revolver — the right-hand side. Nothing else retains it. That is the whole of the published strip: frame, cylinder base pin, cylinder.
steps.prose: It will drop as soon as it clears. Have a hand under it rather than over it.
steps.quote: 4. Slide the cylinder base pin all the way out until it is free of the frame. 5. Remove the cylinder toward the loading gate side of the revolver.
steps.cite: 1873 S.A. CATTLEMAN® SINGLE ACTION REVOLVER AND REVOLVING CARBINE INSTRUCTION MANUAL and safety information — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Cleaning and Maintenance, p.20

steps.title: Wood, aluminium or brass rod — NEVER steel
steps.action: Use a wood, aluminium or brass cleaning rod, a brass bristle brush, and patches sized to your calibre. Uberti rules steel rods out explicitly, and on a replica with a soft blued or case-hardened bore a steel rod is exactly what rings a muzzle crown. Scrub each cylinder chamber and the barrel bore with a good cleaning solution.
steps.prose: Brass polish is the right tool for the backstrap and trigger guard — solid brass parts tarnish and it comes straight off.
steps.quote: To clean your revolver, use a wood, aluminum or brass cleaning rod (do not use steel), a brass bristle brush, and patches that are correctly sized to the caliber of your revolver.
steps.cite: 1873 S.A. CATTLEMAN® SINGLE ACTION REVOLVER AND REVOLVING CARBINE INSTRUCTION MANUAL and safety information — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Cleaning, p.20
steps.warn: No steel cleaning rod on this revolver.

steps.title: Brush all the way through — never reverse inside the bore
steps.action: Push the brush all the way through the bore or the chamber and out the far end before you reverse it. Turning a brush around while it is still inside is how bristles get folded back and how a bore gets scored. Then run clean patches through the bore and every chamber until they come out clean.
steps.prose: Six chambers plus the barrel, and each one needs the same full-length pass.
steps.quote: Always brush all the way through the bore; never try to reverse directions while the brush is actually in the barrel or chamber. After scrubbing, run clean patches through the bore and chambers until they come out clean.
steps.cite: 1873 S.A. CATTLEMAN® SINGLE ACTION REVOLVER AND REVOLVING CARBINE INSTRUCTION MANUAL and safety information — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Cleaning, p.20

steps.title: Completely but lightly oiled — including the grip
steps.action: Oil the entire revolver completely but lightly. Uberti notes that the oil will colour the one-piece grip over the years into a soft patina, so the grip is not a place to keep dry. Check the barrel is clean and free of obstruction before it is loaded again, and clean and oil after every use to prevent corrosion.
steps.prose: Nickel-plated and white-finish guns need more of this, not less: the white finish rusts from the acidity on your hands alone.
steps.aside: Use a good quality brass polish on the back strap and trigger guard.
steps.quote: Thereafter, completely, but lightly, oil the entire revolver. You will find that the oil will nicely color the one piece grip of your revolver over the years and it will develop and retain a soft patina glow.
steps.cite: 1873 S.A. CATTLEMAN® SINGLE ACTION REVOLVER AND REVOLVING CARBINE INSTRUCTION MANUAL and safety information — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Cleaning, p.20

steps.title: The ammunition rule that goes with this action
steps.action: Before it goes back into service: only new commercially loaded ammunition of the correct calibre. Uberti rules out anything marked High Speed or High Velocity and rules out reloaded ammunition entirely, and its own liability disclaimer names hand-loaded and remanufactured ammunition as things it will not answer for. These are replicas of 1873 designs proofed at the Italian National Proof House, not modern magnum frames.
steps.prose: The pressure ceiling is the point. A .45 Colt loaded to modern heavy standards is not what this frame was proofed to.
steps.quote: (WARNING: Do NOT use ammunition marked “High Speed” or “High Velocity” and NEVER use reloaded ammunition.)
steps.cite: 1873 S.A. CATTLEMAN® SINGLE ACTION REVOLVER AND REVOLVING CARBINE INSTRUCTION MANUAL and safety information — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Loading, p.18

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, cylinder base pin, cylinder. That is the entire teardown this manual publishes for an 1873 Cattleman and it is enough to reach the bore, all six chambers, the cylinder faces and the frame window. Put it back by reversing it, then check the base pin screw has caught and the cylinder indexes at half cock.
steps.prose: There is no published lockwork procedure here, so there is no Deep Clean to walk.
steps.quote: 5. Remove the cylinder toward the loading gate side of the revolver.
steps.cite: 1873 S.A. CATTLEMAN® SINGLE ACTION REVOLVER AND REVOLVING CARBINE INSTRUCTION MANUAL and safety information — ABSENT — no revision, date code or edition statement printed anywhere in the document. — Cleaning and Maintenance, p.20

deepAbsentReason: Uberti publishes NO deeper procedure in this book. Its CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE chapter contains exactly one disassembly — REMOVING THE CYLINDER, five numbered steps — and then a CLEANING section that assumes the revolver in that state. Nothing in the document describes taking the grip, backstrap, trigger guard, hand, bolt, mainspring or hammer out, and the four safety systems it describes (retracting firing pin, hammer safety bar, cylinder base pin safety, transfer bar) are described as mechanisms to be understood and engaged, never as assemblies to be stripped. The warranty section separately voids cover where 'an unauthorized repair and/or alteration has been performed'. There is therefore nothing published to walk, and a single-action lockwork teardown — a mainspring and four leaf-spring-driven parts under tension behind the grip frame — would be invented rather than sourced.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBERS
tasks: Wood, aluminium or brass rod ONLY — never steel
Brass bristle brush and correctly sized patches
Good quality cleaning solution through the barrel bore and each of the six chambers
Brush all the way through before reversing — never turn it round inside the bore
Patches until they come out clean

cleaning.name: CYLINDER & BASE PIN
tasks: Clean the cylinder face, the ratchet and the base pin bore
Clean the base pin itself and the frame hole it runs in
Never remove or install a loaded cylinder
Check the base pin is straight before it goes back in

cleaning.name: FRAME & FURNITURE
tasks: Completely but LIGHTLY oil the whole revolver, grip included
Good quality brass polish on the backstrap and trigger guard
White-finish guns: oil after handling — hand acidity alone will rust them
Check the barrel is clean and free from obstructions before loading

reassembly: Fit the cylinder back into the frame from the loading gate side, lining its bore up with the base pin hole.
Slide the cylinder base pin in from the muzzle end, through the frame and the cylinder, until it is fully home.
Old Model / Black Powder frame: tighten the cylinder base pin screw. New Model / Prewar frame: release the spring-loaded screw and let it snap into the pin's groove.
Tug the base pin forward to confirm it is retained before anything else.
With the hammer at half cock, rotate the cylinder a full revolution and check it turns freely and indexes.
Lower the hammer onto an empty chamber, and leave an empty chamber under the hammer for carry or storage.
fncheck: With the revolver empty, bring the hammer to half cock and turn the cylinder a full revolution: it must rotate freely, index cleanly at each chamber, and lock up when the hammer is brought to full cock. Tug the base pin forward and confirm the screw has retained it — a base pin that walks under recoil releases the cylinder. Then practise lowering the hammer on the empty gun as the manual instructs: keep firm rearward pressure on the spur, pull the trigger, ease it past half cock and release the trigger before letting it click into the quarter cock position. If your revolver has the cylinder base pin safety, engage it and confirm the hammer is mechanically blocked before you trust it — it is a manual safety and it is not always on.
